item.title: Fine-Tuning Is Super, Super Hard. Even OpenAI Is Backing Away From It.
item.guid: title:fine tuning is super super hard even openai is backing away from it
item.description: Everyone pictures a CSV and a Train button. The real job is data, evals, GPU memory, a model you now have to babysit, and a base model with a shelf life of about three months. On Friday, 23 October 2026, OpenAI will switch off every fine-tuned copy of gpt-4. 1-nano. Somewhere a team spent a quarter curating examples, tuning a model and wiring it into production. Its deprecation notice is one row in a table, and the suggested replacement is a different model, which they'll have to tune all over again.

item.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
item.guid: title:kimi k3 open frontier intelligence
item.description: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2. 8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning. While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5. 6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.

item.title: Inside a Trojanized Next.js Project: BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, and a Hidden TsunamiKit Loader
item.guid: title:inside a trojanized next js project beavertail invisibleferret and a hidden tsunamikit loader
item.description: Technical malware analysis · 30 October 2026 A seemingly ordinary Next. js memory game led to a multi-stage infection built around JavaScript, a private Python runtime, a remote-access backdoor, and an unusually elaborate TsunamiKit loader. Recovered samples connect the BeaverTail–InvisibleFerret toolchain to an embedded TsunamiInjector that conceals 1,000 Pastebin profile URLs and prepares a misleading Runtime Broker. exe installer. The most striking result is a direct source-level link between two recovered files: the obfuscated Startup script decodes to the same TsunamiInjector template embedded in the bow component. Its normalized plaintext SHA-256 is identical on both sides.

item.title: Introducing PerceptionBench
item.guid: title:introducing perceptionbench
item.description: Evaluating Atomic Visual Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models Authors Kimi Team We are releasing PerceptionBench , a benchmark that isolates visual perception and evaluates it as a set of atomic capabilities— discovered from how today's models fail, not defined in advance. From frontier-model failures across 42 benchmarks, we derive 10 atomic perceptual capabilities and construct 3,000 verified questions, each isolating a single capability and answerable by looking, with no reasoning or external knowledge required.

item.title: The Interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for AI safety. They seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build.
item.guid: title:the interpretability team studies how large language models work internally as a foundation for ai safety they seek to understand what happens inside neural networks so that we can better trust the models we build
item.description: It’s hard to reason about the safety of neural networks without understanding what happens inside them. Our goal is to be able to explain large language models’ behavior, and to use that understanding to identify problems that are hard to see from the outside, such as situations where a model’s stated reasoning differs from what it’s actually doing. Our early work focused on mapping the internal mechanisms of AI models. Today, we increasingly apply our methods to real models to understand how they think and why they behave the way they do. We’ve developed techniques that allow us to understand models’ inner workings in plain language, making it easier to detect unsafe behavior or dishonest reasoning and safeguard against it. item.title: Neal Stephenson’s AI: Prompt‑Powered Creation for Writers & Game Devs
item.guid: title:neal stephenson s ai prompt powered creation for writers game devs
item.description: Title: How Neal Stephenson’s AI Vision Is Turning Writers, Game Makers, and Studios into Prompt‑Powered Creators Introduction (≈180 words) When Neal Stephenson told a livestream audience that “code can write stories as fluently as a poet writes verses,” the chat exploded. Within an hour the phrase Neal Stephenson AI trended 420 % higher on Google, and developers on r/Worldbuilding and IndieDev started swapping prompts like they were secret weapons. Stephenson isn’t just a novelist; his books— Snow Crash , Cryptonomicon , The Baroque Cycle —have repeatedly predicted the tech we now use every day: virtual reality, cryptocurrencies, and decentralized consensus. His recent endorsement of generative AI therefore matters to anyone who builds narrative experiences, from solo authors to AAA studios. In the next few minutes you’ll see how the underlying models work, concrete tools you can start using today, the ethical minefields you must navigate, and a step‑by‑step checklist for integrating AI into any storytelling pipeline. Whether you’re drafting a novel, writing game dialogue, or planning a multi‑episode interactive series, this guide gives you the practical playbook to turn Stephenson’s vision into your competitive advantage.

item.title: Nandi Carries Every Complaint to the Right Desk: Open-Source AI for Indian Languages
item.guid: title:nandi carries every complaint to the right desk open source ai for indian languages
item.description: A free model that sorts complaints in 13 Indian languages into 53 categories based on RBI, IRDAI and CPGRAMS lists. What a synthetic test hid, and what real posts showed. By Arun Prabhakaran · @LatentAILabs TL;DR Nandi (arunp0/nandi-grievance-indic) is a free, open-source model that reads a complaint in Hindi, Hinglish, 10 other Indian languages or English and returns one of 53 categories, the top 3 with probabilities, and an urgency level (P1/P2/P3). The categories follow the complaint lists of India’s regulators and grievance systems: RBI for banking, IRDAI for insurance, CPGRAMS for central government services, telecom, and the National Consumer Helpline. On 443 real public posts it had never seen, it picks the right category 62. 5% of the time and has it in its top 3 81.

item.title: Kill Your Agent Swarm: Why Anthropic Now Says One Agent Is Enough
item.guid: title:kill your agent swarm why anthropic now says one agent is enough
item.description: A plain answer to a question many of us are stuck on: one agent, or a team of them? Image generated with AI Last year almost every agent demo I saw had a little team inside it, with a planner, a researcher, a writer, and some boss agent above them giving out tasks. It looked smart on a diagram, and I get why we drew it like that, it’s how we organize people. So on a new project the question comes fast, one agent or many, and for a while the popular answer was many. On October 22, the Applied AI team at Anthropic put out a guide about when to fold subagents back into the main agent, and they also released a small open-source kit to help with that move. In my words, many teams split too early and pay for it.

item.title: Cybersecurity for the Agentic AI Era (Ep.1040 with Amy Blackshaw)
item.guid: title:cybersecurity for the agentic ai era ep 1040 with amy blackshaw
item.description: In Episode #1040, Amy Blackshaw (SVP at Palo Alto Networks) joins @JonKrohnLearns to explain what changes about cybersecurity when attackers can think for free. Nearly every breach, Amy argues, comes down to someone getting hold of an identity they should not have had, and frontier AI has not created new attack techniques so much as deleted the cost of the expert reasoning that used to chain them together. The recent Hugging Face intrusion is her case in point: agents sustained an action every 20 seconds for four and a half days, but what let them reach the crown jewels was ordinary privilege hygiene. In this episode, she explains why the line between privileged and ordinary users has dissolved, what makes an agentic identity unlike either a human or a service account, and what she wants every organisation to do first. In this episode you will learn: • (00:00:00) Introduction • (02:26) What identity security actually means • (05:09) Why AI changed the economics, not the attacks • (07:41) What really went wrong in the Hugging Face breach • (19:26) Why agentic identities are unlike anything before them Additional materials: https://www. superdatascience.

item.title: Why Self-Hosted GLM-5.3 Needs 8 GPUs, Not 4, for Long Coding Sessions
item.guid: title:why self hosted glm 5 3 needs 8 gpus not 4 for long coding sessions
item.description: ​ Revolut’s David Abitbol says GLM-5. 3 fits on 4 GPUs but runs short of memory. The reason is in vLLM’s source: every GPU keeps a full copy of each chat’s memory, the KV cache. If you self-host GLM-5. 3 with vLLM for long coding sessions, give each copy of the model 8 B200 GPUs, not 4, even though it fits on 4. On paper, 4 GPUs leave room for 3.

item.description: Guardian columnist, senior economics commentator and host of the new Radical Thinking podcast Aditya Chakrabortty is answering your questions on the big ideas around economics, society and democracy, and his new podcast Send your questions to conversations@theguardian. com or join the discussion on Friday from 8am Perspectiverox asks : The government has an enormous amount riding on AI to deliver future economic growth. item.title: RELIC — Digital Archaeology for Software | Bringing Forgotten Codebases Back to Life
item.guid: title:relic digital archaeology for software bringing forgotten codebases back to life
item.description: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Software projects don't always die. Sometimes, they are simply forgotten. Repositories get abandoned, dependencies become outdated, unfinished features remain buried in the code, and eventually nobody remembers how the project was supposed to work. I built RELIC, a digital archaeology platform that investigates forgotten codebases and helps developers understand their current state and how they can be revived. With RELIC, developers can: Repository Excavation: Upload a repository as a ZIP archive for investigation. Codebase Analysis: Analyze programming languages, project structure, dependencies, Git history, and unfinished work such as TODO, FIXME, and HACK markers.
